# Transient synovitis

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Pediatric orthopedics and trauma > Transient synovitis*

[Original Article Link](/library/-v0DcR)

---

## Summary

Transient <u>synovitis</u> is characterized by nonspecific inflammation and <u>hypertrophy</u> of the <u>synovial membrane</u> of the <u>hip joint</u> and is a common cause of acute, nontraumatic <u>hip pain</u> and/or <u>limp in children</u>. Transient <u>synovitis</u> is <u>self-limited</u> and is associated with recent viral infection. Clinical features include <u>antalgic gait</u>, groin <u>pain</u>, and limited painful hip motion. Transient <u>synovitis</u> is a <u>clinical diagnosis</u> supported by diagnostic tests to rule out <u>septic arthritis</u> and other <u>common causes of hip pain in children</u>. Treatment is supportive and consists of rest and <u>NSAIDs</u>. Symptoms typically improve within 24 hours and resolve within 2 weeks.

---

## Epidemiology

* Common cause of acute, nontraumatic <u>hip pain</u> and/or <u>limp in children</u> [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)[[3]](/library/bWdHPK0)

* Peak <u>incidence</u>: 3–8 years of age [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Sex: <u>♂</u> > <u>♀</u> (2:1) [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)




Epidemiological data refers to the US, unless otherwise specified.

---

## Etiology

* Exact cause is unknown. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Associated with recent viral <u>upper respiratory infection</u> and <u>gastroenteritis</u> [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)[[3]](/library/bWdHPK0)

---

## Pathophysiology

Nonspecific inflammation and <u>hypertrophy</u> of the <u>synovial membrane</u>

---

## Clinical features

* Onset of symptoms over 3–5 days [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Well-appearing; possible low-grade <u>fever</u> [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Unilateral groin <u>pain</u> that may radiate to the <u>medial</u> thigh, buttock, and/or knee [[3]](/library/bWdHPK0) [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Examination findings [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0) [[3]](/library/bWdHPK0)

* <u>Antalgic gait</u> and/or refusal to bear weight

* Hip usually flexed, <u>abducted</u>, and <u>externally rotated</u>

* Limited <u>range of motion</u> with <u>pain</u> at the limit of the <u>range of motion</u> of the hip

---

## Diagnosis

Diagnosis is clinical. Diagnostic testing is indicated to rule out alternative diagnoses, particularly <u>septic arthritis</u>. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)[[3]](/library/bWdHPK0)




* <u>Laboratory studies</u>

* Indication: to assess for evidence of infection

* Findings: <u>CBC</u>, <u>ESR</u>, <u>CRP</u>, and serum <u>procalcitonin</u> are typically normal.

* Imaging [[4]](/library/EDd8TH0)

* <u>X-ray</u> (e.g., <u>anterior</u>-<u>posterior</u> <u>pelvis</u> and bilateral <u>frog-leg lateral</u> views)

* Indications: to assess for bony causes of <u>pain</u> and/or limp, <u>sacroiliac joint</u> evaluation

* Findings are usually normal.

* <u>Ultrasound</u> of the hip (including <u>POCUS</u>)

* Indications: to assess for effusions or for imaging-guided hip <u>aspiration</u>

* Findings: <u>joint effusion</u>

* <u>MRI</u>: rarely performed as an initial study

* Indications: to assess for infection, <u>tumor</u>, or diagnostic uncertainty

* Findings: <u>joint effusion</u> [[3]](/library/bWdHPK0)

* <u>Arthrocentesis</u> with <u>synovial fluid analysis</u>

* Obtain urgently in all patients with suspected infection, e.g.: [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* <u>Clinical features of septic arthritis</u> (e.g., <u>non-weight bearing</u>, <u>pain</u> throughout <u>range of motion</u>, ill-appearing)

* Elevated <u>ESR</u>, <u>CRP</u>, <u>white blood cell count</u>, and/or <u>procalcitonin</u> (see “<u>Diagnosis of septic arthritis</u>”)

* For findings suggesting infection, see “<u>Interpretation of synovial fluid analysis</u>.”





> [!TIP]
> The <u>Kocher criteria for septic arthritis</u> can help assess the <u>probability</u> of <u>septic arthritis</u> vs. transient <u>synovitis</u> based on symptoms and laboratory findings. <u>Arthrocentesis</u> with <u>synovial fluid analysis</u> facilitates definitive diagnosis. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

---

## Treatment

* Reassure patients and caregivers that transient <u>synovitis</u> is benign and <u>self-limited</u>.

* Outpatient, <u>conservative management</u> is usually appropriate. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

* Rest

* <u>NSAIDs</u> as needed for <u>pain</u> relief (for dosages, see “<u>Nonopioid oral analgesia in children</u>”)

* Consider hospital admission for 24-hour observation if the diagnosis is unclear. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)

---

## Prognosis

* Symptoms generally improve within 24 hours and resolve within 2 weeks. [[2]](/library/Zc1Zaf0)[[6]](/library/xDdEgH0)

* Recurs in approx. 20% of affected children [[6]](/library/xDdEgH0)
